chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Pott's disease and the March 1948 operation
summary: Cobb explains the bone fusion operation he entered on March 1, 1948, how a fall and a car injury together caused the disease, and that he stayed out two and a half years.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: : There was a problem there before?
Pott's disease.
: Yes.

Pott's disease came from a lick. Well, I already suffered with my back, I told you, from when I got hit by the car coming out of the theater and running back, and couldn't see (inaudible) and run into the traffic, and the man hit me. All right, I suffered through the years on that. And he come and hit me later. He just added fuel to the fire to make it flame more. And that's what happened.
: Well, then -- then you got to -- have you got matches?
I don't have anything.
: No matches?
They're all gone now.
: I'll get some.
Got some in there? Look at the left of the stove, and you'll see on the box back there.
: Well, when you went in the first time and had the operation, and how long was that?

First time? I went in March 1st, 1948, March 1st, 1948, and I stayed in the hospital, oh, two and a half months, and I come home in a hospital bed and stayed. And I rented a hospital bed, and I stayed in it, and all together it was four months, they said. But the first doctor

gave me no antibiotics, never had any. So infection set in somewhere because I never felt right. Two months of convalescent period I went up to Greenwood Lake. I think I talked about this yesterday. And I didn't feel right.
But what did they have to do in this operation?
They went into my back and made bone replacement. A bone decayed.
Oh, I see.

They thought -- and the first time that they had to take something from a bone from my hip to transplant in there, but they didn't have to do it the first time, but the second time they took a piece of bone from here and put in there and made a fusion. They had to fuse it.

In other words, what happened, I could have laid two years without an operation but stayed quiet, and it would have stopped decaying and healed itself up. But with an operation you can get up faster, supposedly. That's what it was explained to me. So naturally, I wanted to take the fastest route.
Yes. Actually it didn't (inaudible) so much then.
It didn't. And I stayed out two and a half years.
